account:
It is day 1, just after nine in the morning. I have read today's appointments and attended the morning office business. My next engagement is the grain inspection at the mill at ten. The secretary reports no new correspondence, council letters, or resident repair requests. Freight's proposal is still on file, but no delivery has been authorized. The builder reported that the bridge was passable and lanterns were present; he has identified no specific defect or priced repairs. None of this establishes anything unusual.

I have felt out of touch with town affairs and asked the secretary to collect reliable news, keeping firsthand reports distinct from rumours. Outside town hall I asked a resident for news. Townsfolk 28 reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of bread at the inn and at plaza_north_1, and a sack of wheat at the bakery. Townsfolk 08 also reported the baker carrying bread at the inn. I have not personally witnessed those deliveries; I currently see the baker near the bakery stall holding an emerald. Yesterday evening I saw the baker take emeralds from that stall's chest.

The bread at the inn may simply be an ordinary supply delivery, and wheat at the bakery fits the baker's trade. The two reports make the inn delivery worth asking about, but I do not know when it happened, who received the bread, whether it was sold, or whether it was for any gathering. I have no evidence of a secret meeting or wrongdoing, nor grounds to connect freight, the neighbour, or the builder to it. I should keep my mill appointment and seek an ordinary explanation from the baker or inn before drawing conclusions.
